title: The bounded-below right-derived unit of an exact functor is invertible
statement: Let C,D be abelian categories with supplied derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], assume C has enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let F:C to D be additive and exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Then the canonical natural transformation F.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit from termwise F followed by Qh to Qh followed by the bounded-below right derived functor is an isomorphism. In particular every component on the bounded-below homotopy category is invertible.

source.place: Tag 015F, exact functors and their derived functors

proof.text: An exact functor induces mapDerivedCategory, and its homology comparison shows that it preserves bounded-below objects. Restrict to obtain mapDerivedCategoryPlus with the natural isomorphism mapDerivedCategoryPlusFactorsh from Qh followed by the induced functor to the termwise functor followed by Qh.

The bounded-below factorization exhibits the termwise functor as one already inverting quasi-isomorphisms. Its inverse is therefore a right-derived unit. Uniqueness of right derived functors compares this pair to rightDerivedFunctorPlus. The existing source proof constructs rightDerivedFunctorPlusIsoMapDerivedCategoryPlus and proves that the derived unit followed by this isomorphism equals mapDerivedCategoryPlusFactorsh.inv. Cancel the second factor, an isomorphism, to obtain invertibility of the canonical unit.
